- eventually[t_a,t_b](phi) → at least one time in [t_a,t_b] where predicate is true

For "appears within two weeks", we want the first appearance to be by day 14. That fits "eventually" (at least one time in [0,14] where the condition holds).

	| "d_c(low)" # Species is slowly increasing
	| "d_c(high)" # Species is rapidly increasing
	| "-d_c(low)" # Species is slowly decreasing
	| "-d_c(high)" # Species is quickly decreasing

	| globally[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means the predicate is true over the entire interval from day t_a to t_b

Your STL response must conform to the following rules:
[BEGIN RULES]
u : less_than | greater_than | is | derivative_greater_than | derivative_less_than | derivative_is
less_than : s(t) < c # Species s is less than c
greater_than : s(t) > c # Species s is greater than c
is : s(t) = c # Species s is close to c
derivative_greater_than : d_s(t) > d_c # The rate of change of species s is greater than d_c
derivative_less_than : d_s(t) < d_c # The rate of change of species s is less than d_c
derivative_is : d_s(t) = d_c # The rate of change species s is close to d_c
c : s(t_a) | "c(low)" | "c(mid)" | "c(high)" # c is the level of a species, it can be a specific value or generally just low, moderate, or high
d_c : 0 # Rate of change is 0
	| "d_c(low)" # Species is slowly increasing
	| "d_c(high)" # Species is rapidly increasing
	| "-d_c(low)" # Species is slowly decreasing
	| "-d_c(high)" # Species is quickly decreasing
predicate : u | u1 and u2 | u1 implies u2 # You can combine predicates with Boolean operators
temporal_operator : eventually[t_a,t_b]globally(predicate) # This means that between day t_a and t_b, there is a point when the predicate becomes true for the rest of the interval
	| globally[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means the predicate is true over the entire interval from day t_a to t_b
	| eventually[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means there is at least 1 time between days t_a and t_b that the predicate is true

	| "d_c(high)" # Species is rapidly increasing
	| "-d_c(low)" # Species is slowly decreasing
	| "-d_c(high)" # Species is quickly decreasing

	| globally[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means the predicate is true over the entire interval from day t_a to t_b

- Temporal operators like `eventually[t_a,t_b]` or `globally[t_a,t_b]`

2) Then IgG appears later (at some time t2 > t1)

Your STL response must conform to the following rules:
[BEGIN RULES]
u : less_than | greater_than | is | derivative_greater_than | derivative_less_than | derivative_is
less_than : s(t) < c # Species s is less than c
greater_than : s(t) > c # Species s is greater than c
is : s(t) = c # Species s is close to c
derivative_greater_than : d_s(t) > d_c # The rate of change of species s is greater than d_c
derivative_less_than : d_s(t) < d_c # The rate of change of species s is less than d_c
derivative_is : d_s(t) = d_c # The rate of change species s is close to d_c
c : s(t_a) | "c(low)" | "c(mid)" | "c(high)" # c is the level of a species, it can be a specific value or generally just low, moderate, or high
d_c : 0 # Rate of change is 0
	| "d_c(low)" # Species is slowly increasing
	| "d_c(high)" # Species is rapidly increasing
	| "-d_c(low)" # Species is slowly decreasing
	| "-d_c(high)" # Species is quickly decreasing
predicate : u | u1 and u2 | u1 implies u2 # You can combine predicates with Boolean operators
temporal_operator : eventually[t_a,t_b]globally(predicate) # This means that between day t_a and t_b, there is a point when the predicate becomes true for the rest of the interval
	| globally[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means the predicate is true over the entire interval from day t_a to t_b
	| eventually[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means there is at least 1 time between days t_a and t_b that the predicate is true

[BEGIN RULES]
u : less_than | greater_than | is | derivative_greater_than | derivative_less_than | derivative_is
less_than : s(t) < c # Species s is less than c
greater_than : s(t) > c # Species s is greater than c
is : s(t) = c # Species s is close to c
derivative_greater_than : d_s(t) > d_c # The rate of change of species s is greater than d_c
derivative_less_than : d_s(t) < d_c # The rate of change of species s is less than d_c
derivative_is : d_s(t) = d_c # The rate of change species s is close to d_c
c : s(t_a) | "c(low)" | "c(mid)" | "c(high)" # c is the level of a species, it can be a specific value or generally just low, moderate, or high
d_c : 0 # Rate of change is 0
	| "d_c(low)" # Species is slowly increasing
	| "d_c(high)" # Species is rapidly increasing
	| "-d_c(low)" # Species is slowly decreasing
	| "-d_c(high)" # Species is quickly decreasing
predicate : u | u1 and u2 | u1 implies u2 # You can combine predicates with Boolean operators
temporal_operator : eventually[t_a,t_b]globally(predicate) # This means that between day t_a and t_b, there is a point when the predicate becomes true for the rest of the interval
	| globally[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means the predicate is true over the entire interval from day t_a to t_b
	| eventually[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means there is at least 1 time between days t_a and t_b that the predicate is true
t_a : number | ∞ # Time in days

[BEGIN RULES]
u : less_than | greater_than | is | derivative_greater_than | derivative_less_than | derivative_is

is : s(t) = c # Species s is close to c
derivative_greater_than : d_s(t) > d_c # The rate of change of species s is greater than d_c
derivative_less_than : d_s(t) < d_c # The rate of change of species s is less than d_c
derivative_is : d_s(t) = d_c # The rate of change species s is close to d_c
c : s(t_a) | "c(low)" | "c(mid)" | "c(high)" # c is the level of a species, it can be a specific value or generally just low, moderate, or high
d_c : 0 # Rate of change is 0
	| "d_c(low)" # Species is slowly increasing
	| "d_c(high)" # Species is rapidly increasing
	| "-d_c(low)" # Species is slowly decreasing
	| "-d_c(high)" # Species is quickly decreasing
predicate : u | u1 and u2 | u1 implies u2 # You can combine predicates with Boolean operators
temporal_operator : eventually[t_a,t_b]globally(predicate) # This means that between day t_a and t_b, there is a point when the predicate becomes true for the rest of the interval
	| globally[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means the predicate is true over the entire interval from day t_a to t_b
	| eventually[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means there is at least 1 time between days t_a and t_b that the predicate is true

	| "-d_c(high)" # Species is quickly decreasing

u : less_than | greater_than | is | derivative_greater_than | derivative_less_than | derivative_is

is : s(t) = c # Species s is close to c

derivative_less_than : d_s(t) < d_c # The rate of change of species s is less than d_c

	| "d_c(low)" # Species is slowly increasing
	| "d_c(high)" # Species is rapidly increasing
	| "-d_c(low)" # Species is slowly decreasing
	| "-d_c(high)" # Species is quickly decreasing
predicate : u | u1 and u2 | u1 implies u2 # You can combine predicates with Boolean operators
temporal_operator : eventually[t_a,t_b]globally(predicate) # This means that between day t_a and t_b, there is a point when the predicate becomes true for the rest of the interval
	| globally[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means the predicate is true over the entire interval from day t_a to t_b
	| eventually[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means there is at least 1 time between days t_a and t_b that the predicate is true

[BEGIN RULES]
u : less_than | greater_than | is | derivative_greater_than | derivative_less_than | derivative_is

greater_than : s(t) > c # Species s is greater than c
is : s(t) = c # Species s is close to c
derivative_greater_than : d_s(t) > d_c # The rate of change of species s is greater than d_c
derivative_less_than : d_s(t) < d_c # The rate of change of species s is less than d_c

	| "d_c(low)" # Species is slowly increasing
	| "d_c(high)" # Species is rapidly increasing
	| "-d_c(low)" # Species is slowly decreasing
	| "-d_c(high)" # Species is quickly decreasing
predicate : u | u1 and u2 | u1 implies u2 # You can combine predicates with Boolean operators
temporal_operator : eventually[t_a,t_b]globally(predicate) # This means that between day t_a and t_b, there is a point when the predicate becomes true for the rest of the interval
	| globally[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means the predicate is true over the entire interval from day t_a to t_b
	| eventually[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means there is at least 1 time between days t_a and t_b that the predicate is true

u : less_than | greater_than | is | derivative_greater_than | derivative_less_than | derivative_is

is : s(t) = c # Species s is close to c

derivative_less_than : d_s(t) < d_c # The rate of change of species s is less than d_c

	| "d_c(high)" # Species is rapidly increasing
	| "-d_c(low)" # Species is slowly decreasing
	| "-d_c(high)" # Species is quickly decreasing

	| globally[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means the predicate is true over the entire interval from day t_a to t_b
	| eventually[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means there is at least 1 time between days t_a and t_b that the predicate is true

is : s(t) = c # Species s is close to c
derivative_greater_than : d_s(t) > d_c # The rate of change of species s is greater than d_c
derivative_less_than : d_s(t) < d_c # The rate of change of species s is less than d_c
derivative_is : d_s(t) = d_c # The rate of change species s is close to d_c

	| "d_c(low)" # Species is slowly increasing
	| "d_c(high)" # Species is rapidly increasing
	| "-d_c(low)" # Species is slowly decreasing
	| "-d_c(high)" # Species is quickly decreasing
predicate : u | u1 and u2 | u1 implies u2 # You can combine predicates with Boolean operators
temporal_operator : eventually[t_a,t_b]globally(predicate) # This means that between day t_a and t_b, there is a point when the predicate becomes true for the rest of the interval
	| globally[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means the predicate is true over the entire interval from day t_a to t_b
	| eventually[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means there is at least 1 time between days t_a and t_b that the predicate is true

[BEGIN RULES]
u : less_than | greater_than | is | derivative_greater_than | derivative_less_than | derivative_is
less_than : s(t) < c # Species s is less than c
greater_than : s(t) > c # Species s is greater than c
is : s(t) = c # Species s is close to c
derivative_greater_than : d_s(t) > d_c # The rate of change of species s is greater than d_c
derivative_less_than : d_s(t) < d_c # The rate of change of species s is less than d_c
derivative_is : d_s(t) = d_c # The rate of change species s is close to d_c
c : s(t_a) | "c(low)" | "c(mid)" | "c(high)" # c is the level of a species, it can be a specific value or generally just low, moderate, or high
d_c : 0 # Rate of change is 0
	| "d_c(low)" # Species is slowly increasing
	| "d_c(high)" # Species is rapidly increasing
	| "-d_c(low)" # Species is slowly decreasing
	| "-d_c(high)" # Species is quickly decreasing
predicate : u | u1 and u2 | u1 implies u2 # You can combine predicates with Boolean operators
temporal_operator : eventually[t_a,t_b]globally(predicate) # This means that between day t_a and t_b, there is a point when the predicate becomes true for the rest of the interval
	| globally[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means the predicate is true over the entire interval from day t_a to t_b
	| eventually[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means there is at least 1 time between days t_a and t_b that the predicate is true
t_a : number | ∞ # Time in days

The comparison operators are for whether a species is less than, greater than, or equal to a threshold (c). The c can be specific values or "low", "mid", "high". Also, there are derivative operators for rates of change.

	| "d_c(high)" # Species is rapidly increasing
	| "-d_c(low)" # Species is slowly decreasing
	| "-d_c(high)" # Species is quickly decreasing

Your STL response must conform to the following rules:
[BEGIN RULES]
u : less_than | greater_than | is | derivative_greater_than | derivative_less_than | derivative_is
less_than : s(t) < c # Species s is less than c
greater_than : s(t) > c # Species s is greater than c
is : s(t) = c # Species s is close to c
derivative_greater_than : d_s(t) > d_c # The rate of change of species s is greater than d_c
derivative_less_than : d_s(t) < d_c # The rate of change of species s is less than d_c
derivative_is : d_s(t) = d_c # The rate of change species s is close to d_c

d_c : 0 # Rate of change is 0
	| "d_c(low)" # Species is slowly increasing
	| "d_c(high)" # Species is rapidly increasing
	| "-d_c(low)" # Species is slowly decreasing
	| "-d_c(high)" # Species is quickly decreasing
predicate : u | u1 and u2 | u1 implies u2 # You can combine predicates with Boolean operators
temporal_operator : eventually[t_a,t_b]globally(predicate) # This means that between day t_a and t_b, there is a point when the predicate becomes true for the rest of the interval
	| globally[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means the predicate is true over the entire interval from day t_a to t_b
	| eventually[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means there is at least 1 time between days t_a and t_b that the predicate is true

[BEGIN RULES]
u : less_than | greater_than | is | derivative_greater_than | derivative_less_than | derivative_is
less_than : s(t) < c # Species s is less than c
greater_than : s(t) > c # Species s is greater than c
is : s(t) = c # Species s is close to c
derivative_greater_than : d_s(t) > d_c # The rate of change of species s is greater than d_c
derivative_less_than : d_s(t) < d_c # The rate of change of species s is less than d_c
derivative_is : d_s(t) = d_c # The rate of change species s is close to d_c
c : s(t_a) | "c(low)" | "c(mid)" | "c(high)" # c is the level of a species, it can be a specific value or generally just low, moderate, or high
d_c : 0 # Rate of change is 0
	| "d_c(low)" # Species is slowly increasing
	| "d_c(high)" # Species is rapidly increasing
	| "-d_c(low)" # Species is slowly decreasing
	| "-d_c(high)" # Species is quickly decreasing
predicate : u | u1 and u2 | u1 implies u2 # You can combine predicates with Boolean operators
temporal_operator : eventually[t_a,t_b]globally(predicate) # This means that between day t_a and t_b, there is a point when the predicate becomes true for the rest of the interval
	| globally[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means the predicate is true over the entire interval from day t_a to t_b
	| eventually[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means there is at least 1 time between days t_a and t_b that the predicate is true
t_a : number | ∞ # Time in days

S9F)" refers to a supplementary figure showing this result.

Now, looking at STL rules provided. STL deals with temporal properties of signals over time. Key elements are:
- Species names (like il1α)
- Comparison operators (less_than, greater_than, etc.)
- Derivative operators for rates of change
- Temporal operators (eventually, globally)

The challenge here is that the sentence says "was not detected" - which implies absence or zero concentration. In STL terms, we'd want to express that the signal s(t) = 0 (or very close to zero) throughout some time interval.

Let me break down the sentence:
- "Circulating IL-1α" → species name: il1α (from the s list)
- "also was not detected" → meaning the concentration was zero (or below detection limit)
- "(fig. S9F)" → this is just a citation and doesn't affect translation

Important considerations:
1. In biological contexts, "not detected" usually means concentration is below the detection threshold (which might be set as 0 for simplicity in models).
2. STL uses continuous signals, so we'd model this as s(t) < c(low) where c(low) is the detection threshold (but the rules show c can be "c(low)", "c(mid)", "c(high)").

Looking at the rules:
- is : s(t) = c (close to)
- less_than : s(t) < c
- c can be "c(low)" meaning low concentration level

For "not detected", it's safest to interpret as s(t) being very low (below detection limit). But since STL typically uses strict inequalities for such statements, I should use less_than with c="c(low)".

Temporal aspect: The phrase "was not detected" suggests this holds true over the entire observation period (from start to finish of the experiment). Since it's a single finding (not changing over time), we'd want a global property.

The user mentioned "what parts don't make sense" - I should note that:
- The word "also" is contextual (referring to previous findings) but doesn't add new temporal information.
- The figure reference (fig. S9F) is irrelevant for translation since STL focuses on signal properties, not citations.

Let me check if "not detected" implies something about derivatives? Probably not - if it's not detected at all, the derivative would also be zero (no change). But the sentence is specifically about absence of detection, not dynamics.

Another angle: In some contexts, "not detected" could mean transiently absent, but the phrasing "was not detected" (past tense) suggests a sustained absence. Given the figure reference, it's likely a static finding from one time point or an interval.

The STL example given in rules shows temporal operators with intervals. For this, since it's a single result, we can assume the interval is [t_start, t_end] where t_end is the last measurement time.

But the user didn't specify exact times. In scientific writing, when saying "was not detected" without time bounds, it often refers to the entire experimental period.

I think the cleanest translation is:

Your STL response must conform to the following rules:
[BEGIN RULES]
u : less_than | greater_than | is | derivative_greater_than | derivative_less_than | derivative_is
less_than : s(t) < c # Species s is less than c
greater_than : s(t) > c # Species s is greater than c
is : s(t) = c # Species s is close to c
derivative_greater_than : d_s(t) > d_c # The rate of change of species s is greater than d_c
derivative_less_than : d_s(t) < d_c # The rate of change of species s is less than d_c
derivative_is : d_s(t) = d_c # The rate of change species s is close to d_c
c : s(t_a) | "c(low)" | "c(mid)" | "c(high)" # c is the level of a species, it can be a specific value or generally just low, moderate, or high
d_c : 0 # Rate of change is 0
	| "d_c(low)" # Species is slowly increasing
	| "d_c(high)" # Species is rapidly increasing
	| "-d_c(low)" # Species is slowly decreasing
	| "-d_c(high)" # Species is quickly decreasing
predicate : u | u1 and u2 | u1 implies u2 # You can combine predicates with Boolean operators
temporal_operator : eventually[t_a,t_b]globally(predicate) # This means that between day t_a and t_b, there is a point when the predicate becomes true for the rest of the interval
	| globally[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means the predicate is true over the entire interval from day t_a to t_b
	| eventually[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means there is at least 1 time between days t_a and t_b that the predicate is true
t_a : number | ∞ # Time in days

[BEGIN RULES]
u : less_than | greater_than | is | derivative_greater_than | derivative_less_than | derivative_is
less_than : s(t) < c # Species s is less than c
greater_than : s(t) > c # Species s is greater than c
is : s(t) = c # Species s is close to c
derivative_greater_than : d_s(t) > d_c # The rate of change of species s is greater than d_c
derivative_less_than : d_s(t) < d_c # The rate of change of species s is less than d_c
derivative_is : d_s(t) = d_c # The rate of change species s is close to d_c
c : s(t_a) | "c(low)" | "c(mid)" | "c(high)" # c is the level of a species, it can be a specific value or generally just low, moderate, or high
d_c : 0 # Rate of change is 0
	| "d_c(low)" # Species is slowly increasing
	| "d_c(high)" # Species is rapidly increasing
	| "-d_c(low)" # Species is slowly decreasing
	| "-d_c(high)" # Species is quickly decreasing
predicate : u | u1 and u2 | u1 implies u2 # You can combine predicates with Boolean operators
temporal_operator : eventually[t_a,t_b]globally(predicate) # This means that between day t_a and t_b, there is a point when the predicate becomes true for the rest of the interval
	| globally[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means the predicate is true over the entire interval from day t_a to t_b
	| eventually[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means there is at least 1 time between days t_a and t_b that the predicate is true

Monocyte chemotactic factor chemokine(C-C motif) ligand 2 (CCL2) was increased in the blood of infected patients as well as the transcripts of its receptor CCR2; this was associated with low counts of circulating inflammatory monocytes (Fig. 4I), suggesting a role for the CCL2/CCR2 axis in the monocyte chemo-attraction into the inflamed lungs.

What parts of the sentence make sense to translate and what parts don't? Think carefully, step-by-step through the process, and tell us about how STL could be used to capture the original semantic meaning of the natural language sentence.

Your STL response must conform to the following rules:
[BEGIN RULES]
u : less_than | greater_than | is | derivative_greater_than | derivative_less_than | derivative_is
less_than : s(t) < c # Species s is less than c
greater_than : s(t) > c # Species s is greater than c
is : s(t) = c # Species s is close to c
derivative_greater_than : d_s(t) > d_c # The rate of change of species s is greater than d_c
derivative_less_than : d_s(t) < d_c # The rate of change of species s is less than d_c
derivative_is : d_s(t) = d_c # The rate of change species s is close to d_c
c : s(t_a) | "c(low)" | "c(mid)" | "c(high)" # c is the level of a species, it can be a specific value or generally just low, moderate, or high
d_c : 0 # Rate of change is 0
	| "d_c(low)" # Species is slowly increasing
	| "d_c(high)" # Species is rapidly increasing
	| "-d_c(low)" # Species is slowly decreasing
	| "-d_c(high)" # Species is quickly decreasing
predicate : u | u1 and u2 | u1 implies u2 # You can combine predicates with Boolean operators
temporal_operator : eventually[t_a,t_b]globally(predicate) # This means that between day t_a and t_b, there is a point when the predicate becomes true for the rest of the interval
	| globally[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means the predicate is true over the entire interval from day t_a to t_b
	| eventually[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means there is at least 1 time between days t_a and t_b that the predicate is true
t_a : number | ∞ # Time in days
s : adam17 | albumin | alkp | alt | ast | bcells | cc3 | ccl2 | ccr2 | cd107a | cd19 | cd24 | cd38 | cpg2216 | crp | gcsf | glut1 | glut3 | gmcsf | ifn | ifnα | ifnβ | ifnγ | igg | igm | il10 | il12 | il15 | il17 | il18 | il1ra | il1rn | il1α | il1β | il2 | il27 | il4 | il5 | il6 | il8 | ip10 | lymphocytes | mcp | mcp1 | mcp2 | mcp3 | mcp4 | merscov | mip1a | mip1b | monocytes | mx1 | mx2 | neopterin | neutrophil | ns1 | platelets | rantes | reticulocytes | sarscov | sarscov2 | stat1 | stnfri | stnfrii | tcells | titers | tnfα | triglycerides | virus | vp40 # Species names you can use
d_s : d_adam17 | d_albumin | d_alkp | d_alt | d_ast | d_bcells | d_cc3 | d_ccl2 | d_ccr2 | d_cd107a | d_cd19 | d_cd24 | d_cd38 | d_cpg2216 | d_crp | d_gcsf | d_glut1 | d_glut3 | d_gmcsf | d_ifn | d_ifnα | d_ifnβ | d_ifnγ | d_igg | d_igm | d_il10 | d_il12 | d_il15 | d_il17 | d_il18 | d_il1ra | d_il1rn | d_il1α | d_il1β | d_il2 | d_il27 | d_il4 | d_il5 | d_il6 | d_il8 | d_ip10 | d_lymphocytes | d_mcp | d_mcp1 | d_mcp2 | d_mcp3 | d_mcp4 | d_merscov | d_mip1a | d_mip1b | d_monocytes | d_mx1 | d_mx2 | d_neopterin | d_neutrophil | d_ns1 | d_platelets | d_rantes | d_reticulocytes | d_sarscov | d_sarscov2 | d_stat1 | d_stnfri | d_stnfrii | d_tcells | d_titers | d_tnfα | d_triglycerides | d_virus | d_vp40 # Names for derivatives of the species
[END RULES]

The d_s terms represent the derivative of a signal, so you may find those terms helpful for describing how signals increase or decrease. For general statements describing the levels of some species as "high" or "low" for example, you may find comparison statements helpful.
